ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Figure shows a feedback system where \( K > 0 \). The range of \( K \) for which the system is stable will be given by ______.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure is a single-input single-output negative feedback system, the transfer function inside the forward channel block is K/[s(s+3)(s+10)], the output end returns to the negative terminal of the summing point through a feedback line, and the input enters the positive terminal of the summing point, therefore it is a unity negative feedback structure. Then reason: The unity negative feedback closed-loop characteristic equation is 1 + K/[s(s+3)(s+10)] = 0. Simplifying gives s(s+3)(s+10)+K=0, that is, s^3+13s^2+30s+K=0. Construct the Routh table for this third-order polynomial: the s^3 row is [1, 30], the s^2 row is [13, K], the first element of the s^1 row is (13·30-K)/13=(390-K)/13, and the s^0 row is [K]. Stability requires the first column to all be positive: 1>0, 13>0, (390-K)/13>0, K>0. Combining with the given condition K>0, obtain K<390. Therefore the stable range is 0<K<390.

method.method_draft: From the image, form the closed-loop characteristic equation: 1 + K/[s(s+3)(s+10)] = 0, so s(s+3)(s+10)+K=0, i.e. s^3+13s^2+30s+K=0. Construct the Routh array for this cubic: row s^3: [1, 30], row s^2: [13, K], row s^1: [(390-K)/13, 0], row s^0: [K]. Stability requires all first-column entries positive. With the text condition K>0, this gives (390-K)/13>0, hence 0<K<390.
method.CoT_raw:
先描述图像：图中是一个单输入单输出负反馈系统，前向通道方框内的传递函数为 K/[s(s+3)(s+10)]，输出端通过一条反馈线回到求和点的负号端，输入进入求和点的正号端，因此是单位负反馈结构。

再推理：单位负反馈闭环特征方程为 1 + K/[s(s+3)(s+10)] = 0。化简得 s(s+3)(s+10)+K=0，即 s^3+13s^2+30s+K=0。对该三阶多项式列 Routh 表：s^3 行为 [1, 30]，s^2 行为 [13, K]，s^1 行首元素为 (13·30-K)/13=(390-K)/13，s^0 行为 [K]。稳定要求第一列全为正：1>0、13>0、(390-K)/13>0、K>0。结合题设 K>0，得到 K<390。因此稳定范围为 0<K<390。

method.method_draft: From the diagram, write the closed-loop characteristic polynomial as p(s)=s(s+3)(s+10)+K=s^3+13s^2+30s+K. To find the stability boundary, set s=jω. Separating p(jω)=0 gives real part K-13ω^2=0 and imaginary part -ω^3+30ω=ω(30-ω^2)=0. The nonzero crossing has ω^2=30, so K=13ω^2=390. At K=0 the roots are 0, -3, and -10; for a small positive K, the root near zero moves to approximately -K/30, so the closed-loop poles are in the left half-plane. Therefore the system is stable for positive K before the first imaginary-axis crossing and loses stability at K=390, giving 0<K<390.
method.CoT_raw: Image description: The figure shows a standard single-loop negative feedback system. The summing junction has a plus sign for the reference input and a minus sign for the feedback signal. The forward-path block in the image is K/[s(s+3)(s+10)], and the output is fed back directly with unity gain. Reasoning: For unity negative feedback, the closed-loop characteristic equation is 1 + K/[s(s+3)(s+10)] = 0, so p(s) = s(s+3)(s+10) + K = s^3 + 13s^2 + 30s + K. To find the stability boundary, set s = jω. Then p(jω) = (jω)^3 + 13(jω)^2 + 30jω + K. Separating real and imaginary parts gives real part K - 13ω^2 = 0 and imaginary part -ω^3 + 30ω = ω(30 - ω^2) = 0. The nonzero imaginary-axis crossing occurs at ω^2 = 30, giving K = 13ω^2 = 13×30 = 390. At K = 0, the roots are 0, -3, and -10, so K = 0 is a boundary, not a strictly stable case. For a small positive K, the root near zero moves approximately to -K/30, so the poles lie in the left half-plane initially. Therefore the system remains stable for positive K until the first imaginary-axis crossing at K = 390.
